data.name: Soldiers of the Universe
data.detailed_description:
Join the War Against Real Terror!

Soldiers of the Universe is a story-driven first person shooter game that tells the story of a group of soldiers fighting against terrorist organizations in the Middle-East.

Story

The Republic of Turkey has a secret organization called "Akinci Warriors" who specializes in secret military operations. Our hero Hakan takes over his father Selim Kahraman’s place as "The Toyga" of Akinci Warriors. He will lead military operations to take his father’s revenge and he will fight against the enemies of the state. Having trained in military and various branches of science for many years Hakan will be fighting a relentless struggle against terrorists along with three other heroes that joined to his side. After meeting Mr. Barbaros and Akıncı warriors, a lot will change in Hakan's life. He will learn what "patriotism" really means and he will understand the importance of fighting for his own country but not for his personal devils. With the intelligence gathered by Republic of Turkey, The Military and Akinci Warriors; our heroes will carry out operations against various terror organizations at Southeast Anatolia, Northern Syria and Istanbul.

Operation Locations

• Cizre / Sirnak / Turkey
• Nusaybin / Mardin / Turkey
• Jarabulus / Aleppo / Syria
• Al-bab / Aleppo / Syria
• Sultanahmet / Istanbul / Turkey

Development Process

This is the first game of a handful devoted indie game developers at Rocwise Entertainment. We worked for countless days and nights to make it possible to put up this story-driven FPS game of ours within a few months on a tight budget.

After finishing concept, design and story elements in February 2017, development process of Soldiers of The Universe (SoTU) finally came to an end. Initially, we were planning to release SoTU in July 2017. But to make a smooth launch and more importantly, to get face to face feedback from the players, we decided to postpone our release date to match with the first day of GameX 2017 International Digital Gaming and Entertainment Expo.

*Visuals, gameplay mechanics and animations on this page does not represent the final quality of the experience.

reviews.review:
I received this product for free. Wish I hadn't. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iOSbfclBaoo

Soldiers of the Galaxy has a lot going against it before you even accept to review it like an idiot. 

The nonsense bombastic name, the impenetrable story with some whiffs of nationalism, the fact that it's a modern warfare FPS developed by nobodies - the odds were stacked against from the get go. 

So I start the campaign game, and the intro is both silly and awful. I press F12 to take a screenshot.

This skips the cutscene. 

Luckily, I'm immediately thrown into an another cutscene where four nearly identical soldiers (two of them even feature face masks) on a helicopter introduce themselves by their stupid bird-themed codenames, which they shorten to nicknames. These TIER 1 OPERATORS introduce themselves to each other on the flight to the mission area, even stating their specialties. This is how operations are carried out in real TIER 1 OPS LAND. 

So, I’m dropped off with three AI buddies. The environment is brown and horrible and the level is basically a long corridor bordered by badly modeled and badly textured ruins. 

The level is then populated with enemies that fire at you at full auto and at all times. They will pause and crouch to reload before resuming magdumping at you. They'll do it basically outside of draw distance, too. However, the enemies are all armed with AKS-74Us, with the expected videogame AKS-74U accuracy. So you will have hard time discerning the direction of the shots. 

The damage will super random, sometimes bypassing armor, sometimes not harming you at all. I’ve survived with an empty health bar a few times, too.  

One thing that isn’t random will is the sound of full auto fire that will only cease when you kill the enemies (the AI may or may not do it for you, so here's one thing where this game is better than some other game, namely, Legendary). I don’t know what’s worse: the sounds of fire, or the sounds of bullets hitting the area around you.

So, imagine you’re an idiot playing this game (me) and you’re trying to kill a terrorist. You're aiming at him down the sights. However, if you can see the enemy, they can see you too, and if they AI isn't glitching out, he’s shooting at you. And when you're hit, the sights hop around the screen like crazy. So either you clip the enemy at extreme range while their accuracy poses little threat to you, wait for them to reload, or just fire away, hoping to score a headshot. 

Don't be afraid to fire wildly, your comrades will always give you full ammo and 5 grenades when asked. Specifically, one of them will restock ammo when you press E next-to-but-not-facing-them-or-away-from-them. You can't pick up ammo or guns from enemies. 

They really worked on the reloading animations, they look real smooth, even if nothing else in the game does! I think the devs might have bought the guns and their animations as assets, since the level of work put in them outshines anything else in the game. 

OK, where were we? Oh yeah, running down brown corridors filled with stationary enemies spraying bullets at you like the poorest man's version of poor man's Portal turrets. Sometimes, you will be hit by bullets coming from random direction of the level, because the enemies, triggered even outside of draw distance (in 2017) will still fire at you, the intentions of level designers be damned. 

Speaking of level designers: invisible walls. While the (horrible, badly textured) ruins lining the corridor can sometimes be entered, there's really no reason to, since they offer no alternate routes, no ammo or armor pick ups (the game sorta features armor, but the only way to regain it is to reload checkpoints), no tactical possibilities - nothing! Unless you count invisible walls appearing in doorways and other seemingly traversible areas at random as something. 

Eventually, you get to the end of level and achieve some objective you don't understand the reason for pursuing. Then you get to do the same in some other badly designed level - but you might get a new weapon!

This game is bad and people giving it thumbs up should feel bad. They’re either the family members of the developers, Chinese spambots that spontaneously gained some sort of semblance of self awareness or alien infiltrators trying to build up a cover story by commenting on human entertainment products in some approximation of English. 

Soldiers of the Universe doesn't demonstrate potential, hard work, clever ideas, attention to detail, good story writing, level design talent, or effort put into AI. It's just some indie devs looking at Call of Duty: Modern Warfare and deciding tjat they, people with no training or financing, can do something that Medal of Honor or even other Call of Duty games couldn't do. 

Don't buy it. Don't buy it in a sale. Don't accept it for free. Don't accept it even if someone offered sexual favors. Don't inflict it on your mortal enemies. Don't use it to torture ISIS fighters. 

Just... don't.
